backtest.brier_definition: sum over classes of (probability - outcome)^2, averaged: 0 perfect, 2 worst; a 1/3 guess scores 0.67 for three classes; 0.5 for a yes/no 50/50 guess
backtest.note: Most origins are reconstructed (later measurements of models released by then), so scores are approximate; real point-in-time origins exist only from Jun 2025. Neighbouring forecasts overlap in time: see the non-overlapping and bootstrap results.

data.source: METR time horizons (Time Horizon 1.1 current; 1.0 legacy), as published in Epoch AI's benchmark data (monthly Wayback captures = point-in-time vintages)

limitations: Measures software-task completion under METR's benchmark conditions, not general intelligence or capability in every domain.
Few real point-in-time vintages: most backtest origins are reconstructed, so scores are approximate.
Neighbouring test forecasts overlap in time; the non-overlapping subset is small, so differences can be luck.
Only evaluated models are seen: labs and models METR has not measured are missing (selection bias).
Horizons above 16 hours are near the top of METR's task suite: their CIs are wide and they are left out of trend fits.
The v1.0 to v1.1 bridge rests on a handful of models measured under both suites, and is not used before v1.1 was published.
The underlying trend is model-estimated, not observed; it is scored against the same smoother run on later data.
External signals (Epoch AI models data) exist only as today's file, so their tests are approximately point-in-time.
